name: Staffordshire figures
summary: Earthenware figures from Staffordshire: small folk figures, then Victorian flatbacks of heroes, royals and dogs. A lead glaze and bold enamel colours make a cheap mantelpiece figure for the home.

philosophy.core_thesis: A figure for every mantelpiece comes from a plaster mould and a clear glaze: flat, bold and cheap, it puts a hero, a king or a dog in a poor man's house.
design_principles: Press the figure in a two-piece plaster mould, and use a flat back for the flatback form.
Use a white or cream earthenware, and cover it with a clear lead glaze.
Paint with bold, flat colours: blue, red, green, yellow and black, with gilt on the details.
Make the figure 15 to 40 cm high, with a simple base that carries a name in relief or in gilt.
Choose a subject for the public: a royal, a soldier, a preacher, a murderer, a pair of spaniels.
Pair the figures, as a left and a right, to flank the clock on the mantelpiece.
Give a spaniel a white coat with red or black patches, a gilt chain and a padlock.
Fire the enamel colours in a third firing at about 700 °C.
anti_patterns: A fine thin porcelain body with a delicate lace skirt
A refined shaded modelling of the face with no outline
A figure with a full back and no pair
A pale pastel palette with no black outline
A hand-made single art piece with no mould line

form.shape: Figures of people, animals and groups, often in pairs; the flatback is flat behind and meant to stand against a wall.
form.profile: A simple, rounded outline with a short body and a large head; a pair of spaniels sits face to face with raised chests.
form.foot_and_rim: A low, flat or scrolled base; the flatback has a flat, unglazed or thinly glazed back and a small vent hole.
form.proportion: Height 15 to 40 cm; the wall is 4 to 6 mm thick, and the head is about one fifth of the height.
rules: Press the front in a mould and keep the back flat for the flatback.
Make the left and right figures a pair.
Keep the modelling simple, with bold folds and a clear outline.
Name the subject on the base.
Use clear, flat enamel colours with gilt for details.

bodies.rule: Use a white to cream earthenware that is cheap, light and porous. Keep the walls thick enough for rough use, and keep porcelain out.

forming.joins: Arms, heads and props are pressed apart and fixed with slip. The seam is cleaned and the glaze covers it.
forming.details: A small vent hole in the back or in the base, a visible mould seam on the side, and a thin line of gilt on the edge of the base.

glaze.pattern: Flat blocks of colour with black outline: a red coat, a blue skirt, a white face. A dog has a gilt chain and a padlock on the chest.
glaze.gloss: Gloss, about 70 to 90 GU on the lead glaze; the enamel colours are a little lower.
glaze.wear: The enamel colours flake and wear at the edges. The lead glaze crazes in a fine net, and chips show the white clay.

palette.strategy: A white glaze ground with strong flat colours: cobalt blue, iron red, copper green, yellow and black, with gold on the details.

firing.kiln: A coal-fired bottle oven, with a first firing for the biscuit and a second for the glaze, then a muffle kiln for the enamels.
firing.scale: A cottage industry of many small potteries in Burslem, Tunstall and Hanley, with output of thousands of figures a week in the 1850s.
firing.signs: A mould seam, a vent hole in the back, a thin glaze and a slightly blurred enamel line.

pieces.form: Flatback figure of a Queen on a scroll base, with a name in gilt
Pair of spaniels with a gilt chain and padlock, face to face
A bocage group of a shepherd and a shepherdess with a lamb and a tree
Toby jug of a seated man with a tricorn hat and a jug of ale
Early figure of a fiddler on a chair, with slip details

positive: pair of spaniels with gilt chain
clear glaze with flat bold enamel colours
simple moulded folds and black outline
mould seam and vent hole at the back
name in gilt letters on the base

emotion.target_response: A homely, direct warmth: the viewer sees a plain hero or a loyal dog and thinks of a cottage shelf and a family story.

use_cases: an antique or interior set dressing prompt
a folk-art figure in a cheap, bold style
avoid_when: the brief needs a fine white porcelain figure
the brief wants a matt marble look
the brief needs a modern studio ceramic

modifiers.how: Change to a hard-paste porcelain body, thin the walls, add lace and fine enamels, and give the figure an S-curve pose.
Change to a parian body without glaze and make the surface smooth and matt, with a classical pose.
